entries.title: When to bump an event's gallery version
entries.details: New section in Events: bump `begin_event(version=...)` when a value the label reads is dropped, a value's options or `StatSelector` range change, or a `MenuElement` key is renamed/removed. Don't bump for added or reordered values (the next live run resets the event's replay data by itself), dialogue, images, stat changes, conditions or new menu options.

entries.title: call_available_event no longer handles TempEventStorage
entries.details: `TempEventStorage` (deprecated since 0.2.2) is no longer special-cased: `call_available_event` doesn't remove events from it or track `temp_event_blocker` anymore. Use a normal `EventStorage` with `EventSeenCondition()` for one-off events. The class itself stays only so old saves load.

entries.title: EventComposite / EventSelect: first parameter renamed priority → select_type
entries.details: Matches `Event` and `EventFragment`. Positional calls (`EventComposite(EVENT_RANDOM, ...)`) are unaffected; a call that passed `priority=` as a keyword must use `select_type=`. The select type (1/2/3) is not the priority: `PriorityOption` orders events.

entries.title: Bumping an event's gallery version resets only that event
entries.details: A version change used to wipe more than the event: in the "Locations" view every other event of its location, in the category view the whole category (or raise a KeyError). `reset_gallery(location, event)` now resets just the event whenever `event` is given (new `reset_gallery_event(event)`); the group reset is only used by the journal buttons.

entries.title: Constants for event priority (EVENT_BLOCKING/ALWAYS/RANDOM) and end_event types (END_*)
entries.details: `consts.rpy` now defines `EVENT_BLOCKING` (1), `EVENT_ALWAYS` (2), `EVENT_RANDOM` (3) for the first argument of `Event`, `EventComposite`, `EventFragment` and `EventSelect`, and `END_NEW_DAYTIME`, `END_NEW_DAY`, `END_MAP`, `END_NONE`, `END_CUSTOM` for `end_event(...)` (same values as the strings `"new_daytime"`, `"new_day"`, `"map_entry"`, `"none"`, `"custom"`). Numbers and strings keep working; the base game, the wiki and the examples use the constants now. `end_event("map_overview")` was never a known type (it fell back to the map): use `END_MAP`.

entries.title: get_stat_value returns the chosen block in the replay instead of always 100
entries.details: In a replay (and in `no_gallery` events) `get_stat_value` read the top-level kwargs instead of `kwargs["values"]`, so it returned `alt` (100) whatever option the player picked, and the scene always took the high branch. It now reads through `get_value`, like every other getter. If you worked around this by branching on a different value in replays, remove the workaround.

entries.title: Stat ranges: written once on the StatSelector, values filed under the boundary they reach
entries.details: `get_stat_value(key, ranges=None, ...)` / `set_stat_value(...)`: leave `ranges` out and the running event's `StatSelector` range is used, so the label doesn't repeat it (an explicit `ranges` still wins). The gallery now files a value under the **highest range boundary it reaches** (0 below the lowest) instead of the next-higher one: with `[40, 70]`, a live 75 replays as 70 and a live 39 as 0. The scene keeps the raw value. Rule: list the thresholds your branches use and compare with `>=` (`if corr >= 70`), then live and replay take the same path. Check events that branch on `>` or on values that aren't in their range. Replays saved before may still offer an old upper-bound option until the scene is played again. The `key_range` entry `Selectors` promised in `kwargs["values"]` never existed; the wiki is corrected.

entries.title: Every registered event is validated on start and load; after_load_event_check removed
entries.details: The new `check_registered_events()` walks `event_register` on new game and on load and runs `check_event()` on every event, mod events included. An event whose label (`get_event_label()`) doesn't exist is logged (`Label … is missing`) and hidden. Before, only the base buildings listed by hand in `after_load_event_check` were checked, and only on load. `after_load_event_check(location, events, general_event)` is gone; drop any call to it, nothing replaces it.

entries.title: begin_event binds every Person as a speaker; new Person(speaker=...)
entries.details: `begin_event` (via `bind_event_speakers()`) now binds every registered `Person` — mod persons included — to a store variable named by `Person.get_speaker_name()`: the key up to the first `_` (`aona_komuro` → `aona`), or `Person(..., speaker="name")`; `speaker=""` leaves a person unbound. The variable holds the `Person`, so `aona "..."`, `aona.think "..."` and `aona.get_first_name()` all work without `$ aona = Person["aona_komuro"]`. Existing binding lines keep working. A name that is not a valid identifier, is shared by two persons, or already holds a non-speaker store value is not bound and logged once (category `dialogue`); set `speaker=` to fix it.

entries.title: 0.1.x save migration removed: fix_schools, check_old_versions, check_stats_compatibility, Stat._repair
entries.details: Only 0.2.x saves are supported now. Removed from `script.rpy`: `fix_schools()`, `fix_whisper_characters`/`fix_shouting_characters`/`fix_thinking_characters`/`fix_characters`, `check_old_versions()`, `check_stats_compatibility()`; `Stat._repair()` is gone too. `load_schools` now creates the `school` character itself, and `get_school()` no longer falls back to `fix_schools()`. If your mod called any of these, drop the call. `fix_modifier()` stays (it creates the budget and payroll modifiers).

entries.title: Legacy store variables gone: rules, clubs, buildings, quests, goals, tasks and friends
entries.details: New saves no longer get `rules`, `clubs`, `buildings`, `quests`, `all_quests`, `goals`, `tasks`, `task_check` or `category_quest`, and loading an old save now deletes them from the store (new helper `drop_legacy_store_vars(*names)`) instead of resetting them to `{}`. Code that read `store.rules` / `store.buildings` gets a NameError: use `is_unlockable_unlocked(key)` / `UnlockableCondition(key)` for unlock state and `building_manager` for map buildings.

entries.title: Quest system unhooked: quest_manager global removed, Quest*Effect are no-ops
entries.details: The archived quest system had no live hooks left, so they are gone: `quest_manager` (no global anymore, `QuestManager()` is not created), `fix_quests()`, `label load_quests`, and the `check_task_type` calls in `begin_event`, `end_event`, stat changes and the daytime labels. `QuestCompleteEffect`, `QuestVisibleEffect`, `QuestInvisibleEffect` and `QuestActivateEffect` are `@deprecated` and do nothing; the classes only stay so old saves unpickle. Replace `quest_manager.check_task_type(...)` calls with nothing, and quest effects with Situations or Unlockables.

entries.title: end_event logs unknown return types instead of silently using map_entry
entries.details: `end_event(return_type)` knows `"new_daytime"`, `"new_day"`, `"none"`, `"custom"` and `"map_entry"`. Anything else (e.g. the typo `"next_daytime"`) still falls back to `map_entry`, but now writes an error to the log, because the fallback skips the daytime advance. Check your log for `end_event: unknown return_type`.

entries.title: Correction: call replace_event / set_event_label / add_event_conditions in init 2+
entries.details: The earlier note said `init 1` or later. The base game creates all its events in `init 1`, and at the same priority Ren'Py runs `game/mods/…` before `game/scripts/…`, so an `init 1` call finds no event, logs "no event '…'" and the original keeps playing. Use `init 2 python:` (or later) for these calls.

entries.title: replace_event, set_event_label, add_event_conditions: change base events from a mod
entries.details: At load time (`init 1`+, after `set_current_mod`) a mod can change an event it doesn't own. `set_event_label(key, label, title=None)` plays your scene with the original definition. `replace_event(key, Event(..., same key, label="mymod_scene"))` swaps the whole definition in every storage holding the key; the key must stay the same so "seen" and story chains keep working. `add_event_conditions(key, *conditions)` appends conditions. Nothing happens while the mod is off; when two mods change the same key, the one that runs last wins.

entries.title: Events can play a label other than their key (label=)
entries.details: `Event`, `EventComposite` and `EventFragment` take `label=`; it defaults to the key, so nothing changes for existing events. `get_event_label()` returns it and `get_gallery_name()` names the gallery entry after it. For an event whose label differs from its key, a names-file entry for the label wins, then `title=`, then the key's entry.

entries.title: Gallery entries are filed under the scene label (gallery_name kwarg)
entries.details: Events now pass `gallery_name` (the label) next to `event_name` (the key). The gallery, replays and the journal gallery use the gallery name; "seen" and progress keep using the key. Code that read gallery data via `kwargs["event_name"]` should use `get_gallery_name_from_kwargs(**kwargs)`, and look events up for gallery entries with `get_gallery_event(name)` instead of `get_event_from_register`. For events without `label=` both are the same, so stored gallery data stays valid.

entries.title: add_person_relations: family ties for existing persons
entries.details: `add_person_relations("luna_clark", sister_of=["seraphina_clark"])` adds relations to a loaded person without replacing her. Call it in a `register_start_method` loader; it does nothing while the mod is off. Enter ties on both people.

entries.title: EventStorage.remove_event no longer raises KeyError
entries.details: `remove_event(event_id)` deleted the id from all three priority lists and raised a `KeyError` for the two it wasn't in. It now removes it from the one it is in. To swap a base event, prefer `replace_event`.

entries.title: Kinks: player content preferences, register_mod(kinks=[...])
entries.details: Players set each kink to yes, neutral (ask first) or no, in the journal settings and on the mod page. Register yours with `register_mod(..., kinks=[Kink("key", "Title", "Neutral one-line description.")])`. Keys are case-insensitive and shared: if another mod or the base game registers the same key (e.g. `"ntr"`), it is one kink with one setting, and the first text wins (a different one logs a warning). A kink no active source knows counts as not allowed.

entries.title: KinkCondition, kink_check() and the kink prompt
entries.details: Gate an event (or composite, fragment, EventSelect) with `KinkCondition("key", ...)`: it passes unless a kink is turned off, also in replays. An open (neutral) kink is asked about right before the event runs; a declined event is skipped and the storage picks again (priority 1 → 2 → 3), or the player returns to the menu without a daytime change. Composites ask once for every fragment they could roll and turn unavailable when a fragment storage has nothing allowed. Inside scenes: `if kink_check("key"):` asks if needed and returns whether it is allowed; `$ ask_kinks(...)` only asks. `get_available_events` takes `exclude=` event ids.

entries.title: Family relations: Person(relations=...), are_related(), RelationSelector
entries.details: `Person(..., relations={"mother_of": ["soyoon_yamamoto"]})` records family ties; enter them on both people (a missing side is mirrored). Look them up with `get_relations`, `get_relation(a, b)`, `are_related(a, b, relation=None)` and `get_related_persons(person, relation=None)`. Add types with `register_relation_type("stepmother_of", "stepdaughter_of")`. `RelationSelector(key, of, relation=None, alt=None)` rolls a relative of another selected person. Base: Yuki/Soyoon (mother/daughter), Luna/Seraphina (sisters).

entries.title: Fragment labels must end with end_event, never return
entries.details: A fragment label is entered through `call_event`, which returns to the same statement: a plain `return` re-runs the fragment forever. End every fragment with `$ end_event(...)`, which hands over to the next fragment or ends the composite.

entries.title: Test situations cafeteria_crisis and pta_multi_bar_test removed
entries.details: Both were placeholders from building the situation system and are no longer registered. `situation_manager.get_situation("cafeteria_crisis")` now returns `None`: guard it, or move your teasers/pool events to a real situation (e.g. `new_management`). The wiki still uses `cafeteria_crisis` as an example key in code snippets. For the cafeteria itself, use the `building:cafeteria` Unlockable (`UnlockableCondition("cafeteria")`).

entries.title: Old PTA vote overrides removed: ConditionStorage.ignores, veto, VETO
entries.details: Leftovers of the pre-Unlockable vote are gone. `ConditionStorage.ignores` no longer exists. `get_end_choice(*votes)` only knows `"yes"`/`"no"` and returns `"yes"` when at least half voted yes; it no longer returns `"veto"` or counts `"ignore"` as yes. The `VETO` constant is removed. `PTAOverride` remains only as an inert, deprecated stub for old saves: don't use it, it has no effect. To steer a vote, set the faction bars of your Unlockable (`start_base`, `stat_weights`, measures).

entries.title: Generic PTA vote: one speaker per faction, Unlockable vote_comments=
entries.details: After the pitch, `pta_vote_unregistered_1` now has one random member speak for each faction bar (`"Teachers"`, `"Parents"`, `"Students"`), shown in her `pta_vote <level> <Name>` render, saying a stock yes/no line. `Unlockable(..., vote_comments={"Parents": {"yes": "…", "no": ["…", "…"]}})` replaces those lines for your Unlockable; write them for the faction, since the speaker is random. Bars with other keys are counted without a speaker. Speakers and stock lines live in `PTA_FACTION_SPEAKERS` / `PTA_STOCK_VOTE_COMMENTS` (pta.rpy); `get_pta_vote_turn(unlockable, bar_key, vote)` returns one turn. The `vote` pattern on `pta_vote_unregistered_1` is now `pta_vote <level> <name>.webp`.

entries.title: Generic PTA vote speaks an Unlockable's pitch=, no longer its description
entries.details: `Unlockable(..., pitch="…" | ["…", …])` sets what the headmaster says at the Friday meeting in the generic vote scene `pta_vote_unregistered_1`. Before, that scene read every `SituationDescription` line aloud, including journal-only warnings. Descriptions are now journal-only. Without `pitch`, he says one stock line for the `type_key` (`UNLOCKABLE_STOCK_PITCH`). Add a `pitch` to your Unlockables, written as speech to the parents, teachers and student representative at the table. `unlockable.get_vote_pitch()` returns the lines. Story votes with their own scene (`JournalVoteCondition`) are unaffected.

entries.title: Schedule Vote measure names the escrowed vote cost
entries.details: An Unlockable with a money escrow pair (`UnlockableScheduleVoteConditions(MoneyCondition(n))` + cost `MoneyEffect`) now shows the reserved total in its Schedule Vote effect text: "Schedules the PTA vote and sets aside $n: spent if it passes, returned if it fails or is cancelled." Nothing to change in mods; unpaired or cost-free Unlockables keep "Schedules the PTA vote." Mention the cost in your `SituationDescription` as well.

entries.title: TimerEffect starts a timer from an effect list
entries.details: `TimerEffect(key, new_time="today", *options)` calls `set_timer(key, new_time)`, so a resolution, unlock or menu can start the same timer `TimerCondition` and `get_timer` read. Revert restores the previous timer, or removes it if the effect created it; `EffectNoRevert` skips that. Does nothing during gallery replays. Example: the cafeteria Unlockable sets `TimerEffect("cafeteria_construction")` on a won vote so the build week counts from the vote.

entries.title: School Jobs, Student Relationships and the Cafeteria are registered Unlockables
entries.details: `rule:school_jobs`, `rule:student_student_relation` and `building:cafeteria` now exist in `load_unlockables`, so `UnlockableCondition("school_jobs")`, `UnlockableCondition("student_student_relation")`, `UnlockableCondition("cafeteria")` and `is_unlockable_unlocked(...)` with these keys can become true (before, they never resolved). The map building `cafeteria` opens through the unlock (`BuildingOpenEffect`). For map buildings that aren't Unlockables, check `building_manager.is_open(key)` instead of `is_unlockable_unlocked(key)`.

entries.title: Missing-name warnings are off by default; name check runs from the journal
entries.details: Before, developer builds always logged `No display name for '<key>'` when a name lookup (`get_translation`, `get_first_translation`, `Event.get_title`) missed. Now that warning only appears while **Log missing names** is on (journal → Cheats → Debug → Names, stored in `persistent.log_missing_names`). Switch it on while you test a mod's names files. On the same page, **Check names files** runs `tools/validate_names.py` inside the game (also with the `--events` list) and opens the Logs page filtered to category `names`. This only works when the game runs from the repository, because builds don't ship `tools/`.

entries.title: `JournalVoteCondition` can claim a single group member (`group_index=`)
entries.details:
`JournalVoteCondition("sex_ed", group_index = 1)` gates a story vote scene to level 1 of a group only; without `group_index` it still claims every member of the key. Constructing it claims the vote, so the generic vote scene (`JournalNRVoteCondition`) skips that member and keeps running for the others.
New wiki section on writing your own vote scene: roll with `unlockable.roll_votes()` and always finish through `call pta_vote_result(unlockable, end_choice, True)`, which runs the unlock, failure penalty, money refund and frees the vote slot.

entries.title: A blocking threshold whose condition already holds no longer swallows the bar move
entries.details: Before, a bar reaching a `BlockingThreshold` always stopped at its bound, even if the condition was already true; the gate cleared at the next threshold check and the rest of the move was lost. Now it clears on the spot (plain gate: reached + effects; timed gate: hold, timeout effects kept) and the move continues to the next unmet gate. So `set_progress(...)` followed by `change_stat("situation:<key>:<bar>", n)` in one event moves the full `n`. Unmet gates clamp as before. A check registered by an earlier clamp is dropped, so effects don't fire twice. New helpers: `SituationThreshold.pass_fulfilled_gate()`, `SituationManager.discard_threshold_check(key)`.

entries.title: `get_stat_number` reads situation bars; `StartModifier` can start from another situation's bar
entries.details:
The module-level `get_stat_number("situation:<situation_key>:<bar_key>")` now returns that bar's value, the read side of what `change_stat` already did for writes. It works in every state (a completed situation keeps its last value). Unknown situation or bar: reads `0`, one warning per key. `ALL` stays write-only.
The same key works as a start-value source: `StartModifier("+", 0.5, stat="situation:prep:main")` adds bar value x 0.5 at activation. Only `+` is supported for situation sources (self-test 779); a malformed key fails 768. The source may register after your situation, so the bar is looked up at activation.

entries.title: `StartModifier`: `stat` and `condition` can now be combined
entries.details: Correction to the earlier conditional start modifier post: self-test 778 now only rejects `stat` together with a Selector value (both supply the operand). A `condition` can gate a stat entry: `StartModifier("+", 0.5, stat="situation:prep:main", condition=SituationStateCondition("completed", "prep"))`. Entries that were rejected for `stat` + `condition` now load.

entries.title: Situations settle thresholds the start value jumps past (`start_thresholds` / `on_start`)
entries.details:
Before, a start value past a threshold left it unreached forever (thresholds only fire when the bar moves through them). Now `activate()` settles them right after the start values are computed, nearest first:
- blocking, condition unmet: the bars clamp to its bound and it becomes a normal check (a start value never skips a story gate)
- blocking, condition met / auto: marked reached as in play; repeatable ones stay re-armable
Effects of settled thresholds run only in `"fire"` mode. Default for the whole situation: `Situation(..., start_thresholds="skip")` (also on `Unlockable`). Per threshold: `AutoThreshold(..., on_start="fire")` / `BlockingThreshold(..., on_start="skip")`, `None` follows the situation. Invalid values: self-test 797 / 798.
If your situation relied on start modifiers carrying the bar past a blocking threshold, it now stops at that gate until its condition holds.

entries.title: `StartModifier` takes a `condition` and a `Selector` value
entries.details: `StartModifier("+", 21, condition=ProgressCondition("my_chain", 4))` only applies if the condition holds at activation. `value` can be a `Selector`, rolled fresh on every activation: `StartModifier("+", ProgressSelector(...), condition=...)`. One condition per entry, combine with `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`. A non-number roll skips the entry and logs an error. `stat` can't be combined with either (self-test 778; 776 = bad condition, 777 = value neither number nor Selector). Use it to start a situation that joins a running story chain where an old save already is. Internally a `SituationConditionalStartModifier`.

entries.title: Interface sounds are live; new key `journal_entry`
entries.details:
The base game now registers files for every UI key (`game/scripts/ui_sounds.rpy`, files in `game/audio/ui/`). A mod replaces one with `register_ui_sound("choice", "audio/my-click.ogg", volume = 0.8)` from `init 1 python` or later.
New key `journal_entry` (rank 2): plays once when the map is reached after a new journal alert was raised, not on every return while the journal icon stays lit. Anything that goes through `raise_journal_alert` / `notify_situation_journal_alert` triggers it; `JournalAlertManager.take_announcement()` reads and clears the flag.
Opening the journal straight from a map stat/situation row or a notification slip now plays `journal_open`.

entries.title: Ren'Py `menu:` blocks no longer crash with "Name 'title' is not defined"
entries.details: Since the journal-style choice slips, any plain Ren'Py `menu:` statement crashed as soon as the menu was redrawn (the custom `call_menu` decision menus were not affected). Fixed in `screen jr_choice_slip`. If your mod avoided `menu:` or defined a global `title` as a workaround, you can drop that. Brackets inside menu captions are still not interpolated, same as before.

entries.title: Interface sounds: register_ui_sound / play_ui_sound / UISound
entries.details:
Interface moments now have sound hooks on their own `ui` channel (Effects slider): `journal_open`, `journal_close`, `page_turn`, `choice`, `collect`, `gift`, `notify`, `milestone`. A key without a registered file stays silent.
- `register_ui_sound(key, sound, volume=1.0, rank=None)` sets or replaces a moment's sound (paths with a folder resolve into your mod folder).
- `play_ui_sound(key)` in Python, `UISound(key)` in screen actions: `action [UISound("page_turn"), Call(...)]`.
- Your own keys work too. Within 0.6 s a lower-ranked sound is dropped, so one moment makes one sound.

entries.title: Music: map tracks, mood pools under scenes, play_music / stop_music
entries.details:
`config.has_music` is on. Declare a track as `MusicTrack(sound, priority=0, *conditions, loudness=None, end=None)`: `loudness` is the file's measured LUFS (it is turned down to -20 LUFS so all tracks match), `end` stops early without editing the file.
- `register_map_music(map_key, MusicStorage(None, *tracks))`: picked by conditions, played once when a new daytime starts.
- `register_music_pool(key, *tracks)` / `add_to_music_pool("bed", ...)`: shuffled playlists. `begin_event` starts the `bed` pool; in a scene use `play_music("cozy")` or `stop_music(fadeout)` for deliberate silence.
- `register_menu_music(track)` for the main menu.
If your scene played its own track on the `music` channel, it now competes with the bed: call `stop_music()` first or register a pool.

entries.title: Ambience per building and map: register_building_ambience / register_map_ambience
entries.details:
Room tone is now declared like backgrounds: `AmbienceStorage(fallback, *ambiences)` holds `Ambience(sound, priority=0, *conditions, volume=1.0)` candidates; the highest-priority one whose conditions pass plays.
```python
init 1 python:
    set_current_mod('mymod')
    register_building_ambience("mymod_bar", AmbienceStorage(
        Ambience("audio/bar_quiet.ogg", volume = 0.6),
        Ambience("audio/bar_busy.ogg", 1, TimeCondition(daytime = 7)),
    ))
```
`register_map_ambience(map_key, storage)` does the same for a map. Add to a base place with `get_building_ambience("school_dormitory").add_ambience(Ambience(...))`. Paths with a folder resolve into your mod folder. Register at `init 1` or later (the `audio.` names are init-0 defines). Inside a scene: `play_ambience(sound, volume)` / `stop_ambience()`; `end_event` brings the location's sound back. A building without a registration plays its map's ambience. Level your files to -27 LUFS (true peak <= -1 dBTP) and use `volume` only for intent: 1.0 busy, 0.8 outdoors, 0.6 quiet room.

entries.title: Scenes keep the room tone: begin_event ducks ambience instead of silencing it
entries.details:
`begin_event` still stops the `sound` channel, but ambience now runs on its own channels (`ambience_a`/`ambience_b`, mixer `ambience`) and only drops to 35 % under a scene; `end_event` restores and re-resolves it. Replays play the event location's ambience. If your scene relied on silence, call `stop_ambience()` after `begin_event`.

The base audio files moved from `.mp3` to `.ogg` (`game/audio/ambience/empty-room.ogg`, …). `audio.empty_room` and the other `audio.` names are unchanged; a direct `"empty-room.mp3"` still plays through a `config.audio_filename_callback` fallback (it also keeps old saves loading), but switch to the `audio.` name.

entries.title: play_sound(..., loop=True) for room tone is deprecated
entries.details:
`play_sound(sound, loop=False, volume=1.0, fadein=1.0)` stays for one-shot effects (moved from `helper.rpy` to `audio.rpy`, same signature). Looping ambience through it still works but sits on the effects channel, is cut by the next effect and stops when a scene starts. Old:
```python
label mymod_bar ():
    if time.get_daytime() == 7:
        $ play_sound("audio/bar_busy.ogg", True, 1.0, 1.0)
```
New: `register_building_ambience("mymod_bar", AmbienceStorage(...))` at init and drop the call from the label.

entries.title: Asset pack 1.0.3 is out
entries.details:
Paperdoll sprites now use the mood token `surprised` instead of `suprised`. Mods that ship their own paperdoll sprites should rename the token too.

A new asset pack is online. Run `tools/Download Assets.bat` (or `python tools/download_assets.py`) to update `game/images` before testing your mod against the current scripts.

entries.title: Paperdoll mood token renamed: "suprised" → "surprised"
entries.details: The misspelled mood token is gone from every sprite file name and from the scripts. Update `PDAImage(mood = "suprised")` to `mood = "surprised"`, and rename the token in your own paperdoll sprites (e.g. `<char> $ 1 surprised $ follow $.webp`). The old spelling now resolves to no head image.

entries.title: LevelCondition: pass the character as char_obj=
entries.details: `LevelCondition(value, *options, char_obj=None)` takes the character only as a keyword. `LevelCondition("2+", "school")` puts "school" into the options; it only looked right because an unset char_obj falls back to a char_obj in the event kwargs and then to the school. All base gates now use `LevelCondition("2+", char_obj = "school")`; do the same in your mod.

entries.title: Decision menu: documented as a Python call, dialog anchor default
entries.details: `call_custom_menu_with_text(...)` and `call_custom_menu(...)` are Python functions: write `$ call_custom_menu_with_text(...)`, not `call`. Name branch labels in full (`EventEffect("my_event.branch")`). The default `menu_anchor` is `MENU_ANCHOR_DIALOG` (choices right-aligned on top of the dialogue box). Keep at least one choice ungated, otherwise the player is sent back to the map with a dev error.

entries.title: Events can carry their own title (title=)
entries.details: `Event`, `EventComposite`, `EventFragment` and `EventSelect` take `title="…"`, shown in event menus, the journal gallery and the cheat page. An entry for the same id in a names file (`translations.csv`, your mod's `names.csv`) still wins, so a mod can rename a base event. When you move a name to `title=`, delete its CSV line; `python tools/validate_names.py` reports a CSV entry that hides a title.

entries.title: Mod page lists what each mod adds and changes
entries.details: Every register function now records what a mod adds and which base or foreign content it changes. The mod page lists events, situations, collectibles and the rest instead of a bare event count, and flags mods that replace the same thing. Register content through the register functions so it shows up there.

entries.title: Situations can pause and follow the event flag
entries.details: `situation.pause()` / `resume()` (or `situation_manager.pause_situation(key)`) freeze a situation without ending it. `Situation(..., flag = "camp", flag_exclusive = True)` makes a situation follow the global event flag: it pauses while the flag doesn't match. Code that *does* something should check `situation.is_running()`; `state == "active"` is also true while paused.

entries.title: Event flags replace the intro condition
entries.details: One global flag (`set_current_flag(key)` / `get_current_flag()`) decides which events may run. Every event without a `FlagCondition` gets `FlagCondition(None)` and **does not run while any flag is set** (e.g. the intro or a camp). Use `FlagCondition("camp")` for flag-only events and `FlagCondition("camp", exclusive=False)` for both. `IntroCondition` is replaced by `FlagCondition("intro")`; the `override_intro` parameter is removed.

entries.title: Map registry: add buildings and whole new maps
entries.details: `map_manager` holds several maps. Add a location with `register_buildings(Building(...))` and `map_manager.add_building_to_map("school", building_manager.get_building(key))`; build a second map with `map_manager.load_map(Map(...))` and switch the player to it. The building key is the label that runs on click.
